lines.say: This is what the government says happened, what Rozier says happened, and what the documents show so far.

scene.title: Nine Minutes|in New Orleans
scene.sub: United States v. Terry Rozier · E.D.N.Y. · 25-cr-323

lines.say: Chapter one. Nine minutes.

Start with the game. The Hornets were on the road, in New Orleans, against the Pelicans. According to the indictment, Rozier was not on the team's injury report, and Hornets officials did not know he planned to leave early.

scene.title: Not on the injury report
scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: But the grand jury alleges one person did know. Before the game, Rozier told his longtime friend, Deniro Laster, that he would remove himself in the first quarter, due to a supposed injury, and not return.

scene.title: “a supposed injury”
scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: Prosecutors say Laster then sold that information. Two of the buyers, Marves Fairley and an unnamed co-conspirator, agreed to pay him about one hundred thousand dollars out of their expected winnings. In this first indictment, that money is a payment to Laster for the tip. The word bribe comes later.
lines.show: Prosecutors say Laster then sold that information. Two of the buyers, Marves Fairley and an unnamed co-conspirator, agreed to pay him about $100,000 out of their expected winnings. In this first indictment, that money is a payment to Laster for the tip. The word bribe comes later.

scene.title: Approximately $100,000
scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: Then the money moved. According to the indictment, a bettor named Shane Hennen put about sixty-one thousand two hundred dollars on Rozier's unders at one retail sportsbook. One associate alone placed about one hundred seven thousand.
lines.show: Then the money moved. According to the indictment, a bettor named Shane Hennen put about $61,200 on Rozier's unders at one retail sportsbook. One associate alone placed about $107,000.

scene.title: $61,200 on the unders
scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: An under bet is simple. You win if the player does less than the sportsbook expects. Fewer points. Fewer assists. Fewer minutes.

scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: In all, the Justice Department says, the group placed and directed more than two hundred thousand dollars in wagers on Rozier's unders.
lines.show: In all, the Justice Department says, the group placed and directed more than $200,000 in wagers on Rozier's unders.

scene.label: in wagers placed and directed, prosecutors say
scene.src: U.S. Attorney's Office, E.D.N.Y., press release (Oct 23, 2025)

lines.say: And on the court, it played out the way the bettors needed. Rozier scored five points, with two assists and one three-pointer. His season averages were twenty-one point one points, five point one assists and two point six threes.
lines.show: And on the court, it played out the way the bettors needed. Rozier scored 5 points, with 2 assists and 1 three-pointer. His season averages were 21.1 points, 5.1 assists and 2.6 threes.

scene.title: 5 points. 2 assists. 1 three.
scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: Nine minutes and thirty-four seconds, against a season average of about thirty-five point three minutes a game.
lines.show: 9 minutes and 34 seconds, against a season average of about 35.3 minutes a game.

scene.title: March 23 vs. his season average
scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: The Hornets lost the game. And the government says many of the bets paid off.

scene.title: “His team, the Hornets, lost the game.”
scene.src: Gov't opposition to Rozier's motion to dismiss, ECF 144 (Aug 26, 2026)

lines.say: But one number did not cooperate. Four rebounds. Hold on to that number. Both sides now use it to make their case.

lines.say: Chapter two. The cash.
Five days after the game, according to the indictment, Laster traveled to Philadelphia. The grand jury alleges Rozier arranged and paid for that trip.

scene.title: “arranged and paid for”
scene.src: Indictment, U.S. v. Earnest et al., E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 17 (Oct 16, 2025)

lines.say: In Philadelphia, between the late night of March twenty-eighth and the early morning of the twenty-ninth, Fairley allegedly handed Laster tens of thousands of dollars in cash, as payment for the information about Rozier's exit.
lines.show: In Philadelphia, between the late night of March 28 and the early morning of the 29th, Fairley allegedly handed Laster tens of thousands of dollars in cash, as payment for the information about Rozier's exit.

lines.say: Then, the government says, Laster drove hundreds of miles through the night to Rozier's house in Charlotte.

scene.title: “through the night”
scene.src: Gov't opposition to Rozier's motion to dismiss, ECF 144 (Aug 26, 2026)

lines.say: And in the early morning hours of April first, twenty twenty-three, according to the superseding indictment, Laster and Rozier counted the money together.
lines.show: And in the early morning hours of April 1, 2023, according to the superseding indictment, Laster and Rozier counted the money together.

scene.title: Counting the money
scene.src: Superseding Indictment, E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 101 (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: Prosecutors go further. In an August filing, they wrote that Laster and Rozier photographed themselves counting the cash.

scene.title: “photographed themselves counting the cash”
scene.src: Gov't opposition to Rozier's motion to dismiss, ECF 144 (Aug 26, 2026)

lines.say: Remember: Rozier denies knowing about any bets. A photo of money does not tell a jury where the money came from. That question is what the trial is for.

scene.src: Gov't letter opposing severance, ECF 166 (Nov 3, 2026) · Rozier's omnibus motion in limine, ECF 169 (Nov 12, 2026)

lines.say: Chapter three. The arrest.

For two and a half years, Rozier was not charged. A defense filing says the NBA looked into the game, and in January twenty twenty-five said it had found no rule violation, and was cooperating with a federal investigation. Then, on October twenty-third, twenty twenty-five, the FBI made arrests across the country.
lines.show: For two and a half years, Rozier was not charged. A defense filing says the NBA looked into the game, and in January 2025 said it had found no rule violation, and was cooperating with a federal investigation. Then, on October 23, 2025, the FBI made arrests across the country.

scene.cite: U.S. Attorney's Office, E.D.N.Y., press release (Oct 23, 2025)

lines.say: The same indictment named a former NBA player and coach, Damon Jones, and described tips about other games: a Trail Blazers game, a Magic game, and Lakers games. It also described games involving Jontay Porter, the former Raptors player, who had already pleaded guilty.

scene.src: U.S. Attorney's Office, E.D.N.Y., press release (Oct 23, 2025)

lines.say: Rozier pleaded not guilty. The judge is LaShann DeArcy Hall, in the Eastern District of New York.

lines.say: Chapter four. The bribe.

In May twenty twenty-six, the case got heavier. A grand jury returned a superseding indictment, with two new counts against Rozier: bribery in sporting contests, and honest services wire fraud conspiracy.
lines.show: In May 2026, the case got heavier. A grand jury returned a superseding indictment, with two new counts against Rozier: bribery in sporting contests, and honest services wire fraud conspiracy.

scene.title: Honest services
scene.src: Superseding Indictment, E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 101 (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: Honest services means this. Prosecutors allege he schemed to deprive the Hornets and the NBA of his honest and faithful services, through a bribe.

scene.title: “honest and faithful services”
scene.src: Superseding Indictment, E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 101 (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: The new version tells a different story about the injury. It says Rozier really had a lower leg injury near the end of that season. He kept playing on it. But, it alleges, he planned to use that injury as the reason to leave a game early.

scene.title: “a lower leg injury”
scene.src: Superseding Indictment, E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 101 (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: In exchange for an approximately one hundred thousand dollar bribe, the grand jury says, Rozier agreed to withdraw early from a game still to be chosen, and to give Laster a portion.
lines.show: In exchange for an approximately $100,000 bribe, the grand jury says, Rozier agreed to withdraw early from a game still to be chosen, and to give Laster a portion.

scene.title: “an approximately $100,000 bribe”
scene.src: Superseding Indictment, E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 101 (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: And while the game was being chosen, Laster allegedly kept the buyers updated, using encrypted apps.

scene.title: Encrypted applications
scene.src: Superseding Indictment, E.D.N.Y. 25-cr-323, ECF 101 (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: Now, the four rebounds. Of the four stats the indictment lists, rebounds were the only one where he went over his betting line. According to the superseding indictment, because of those four rebounds, not all of the bets won. So after the game, they negotiated the bribe down to about seventy thousand dollars.
lines.show: Now, the four rebounds. Of the four stats the indictment lists, rebounds were the only one where he went over his betting line. According to the superseding indictment, because of those four rebounds, not all of the bets won. So after the game, they negotiated the bribe down to about $70,000.

lines.say: In its August filing, the government put it in one sentence. For taking a bribe in exchange for removing himself early from a professional basketball game so that others could bet on, and profit from, his underperformance, Rozier is charged with four distinct but related crimes.

scene.title: Four counts
scene.src: Gov't opposition to Rozier's motion to dismiss, ECF 144 (Aug 26, 2026)

lines.say: Chapter five. The others.
While Rozier fights the charges, people around this case have been pleading guilty.

scene.src: CBS News / AP (Apr 28, 2026) · Covers (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: In January twenty twenty-six, a bettor named Timothy McCormack was sentenced to two years in prison by Judge DeArcy Hall. The indictment says he and another man bet about forty-one thousand dollars on Rozier's unders that night.
lines.show: In January 2026, a bettor named Timothy McCormack was sentenced to two years in prison by Judge DeArcy Hall. The indictment says he and another man bet about $41,000 on Rozier's unders that night.

lines.say: In April, Damon Jones pleaded guilty to two counts of wire fraud conspiracy, covering this case and a separate rigged-poker case. According to AP, he acknowledged using insider information from relationships he made as a player. His sentencing is set for January sixth.
lines.show: In April, Damon Jones pleaded guilty to two counts of wire fraud conspiracy, covering this case and a separate rigged-poker case. According to AP, he acknowledged using insider information from relationships he made as a player. His sentencing is set for January 6.

lines.say: Then, on May twenty-eighth, Marves Fairley, one of the alleged buyers of Rozier's information, pleaded guilty to seven felony counts across two cases. In court he said: I agreed to pay a player to change their game performance.
lines.show: Then, on May 28, Marves Fairley, one of the alleged buyers of Rozier's information, pleaded guilty to seven felony counts across two cases. In court he said: "I agreed to pay a player to change their game performance."

lines.say: He did not say the name. A prosecutor did. According to Covers, a lawyer for the U.S. Attorney's Office told the court the player Fairley referenced was Rozier. Rozier's attorney disputed that his client was paid to alter his play.

scene.src: As reported by Covers (May 28, 2026)

lines.say: Fairley's own sentencing is expected in February. Under his plea, he faces up to twenty years on six of the counts, and he agreed to a six hundred seventy-six thousand seven hundred dollar penalty, according to Covers.
lines.show: Fairley's own sentencing is expected in February. Under his plea, he faces up to 20 years on six of the counts, and he agreed to a $676,700 penalty, according to Covers.

scene.label: agreed penalty · up to 20 years on 6 counts

lines.say: So some of the people accused of buying the information, or betting on it, have pleaded guilty. Rozier has not. He says he never knew about any bets.

scene.src: Covers (May 28, 2026) · Rozier's omnibus motion in limine, ECF 169 (Nov 12, 2026)

lines.say: Chapter six. His side.
Rozier's defense, as the government itself summarizes it, is simple. He did not know about any bets. He left the game because he was hurt.

scene.title: “He did not know about any bets.”
scene.src: Gov't letter opposing severance, ECF 166 (Nov 3, 2026)

lines.say: His lawyers say the objective evidence backs him. Unlike every other individual charged in this sweeping conspiracy, they wrote, he never placed a bet on an NBA game or player prop, and he had no knowledge that anyone else was betting on his performance.

scene.q: he never placed a bet on an NBA game or player prop, and he had no knowledge that anyone else was betting on his performance.
scene.cite: Rozier's omnibus motion in limine, ECF 169 (Nov 12, 2026)

lines.say: They point to three things. Medical evidence that he was genuinely injured. The rebounds: he beat that line, the opposite of what the bettors wanted. And one text message.

items: medical evidence of a genuine injury
scene.src: Rozier's omnibus motion in limine, ECF 169 (Nov 12, 2026)

lines.say: Remember the nickname. Chum. While in Philadelphia, Laster texted a third person: Dont tell Chum bout the bet.
lines.show: Remember the nickname. "Chum." While in Philadelphia, Laster texted a third person: "Dont tell Chum bout the bet."

lines.say: The defense says that text guts the case. Why hide a bet from the man who supposedly sold it?

lines.say: The government says its investigation developed evidence from multiple sources that this text chain does not relate to sports gambling. According to the defense, prosecutors now say it was about table games at a casino.

lines.show: Rozier and Laster also asked to be tried separately. The government opposed it, calling Rozier's defense, in effect, an argument that no crime occurred, and asked to keep the joint trial, about three weeks long, starting February 8, 2027.

lines.show: The headline claim: in April 2023, about two weeks after the Pelicans game, Laster allegedly texted Fairley that he and Rozier were setting up another under bet, this one involving one of Rozier's then-teammates.
